headline: Earnings dip on cost pressures, guidance reaffirmed
summary_short: GAAP EPS was $0.65 in Q2 2026, down 4.4% y/y and 25.3% q/q, as higher O&M and financing costs outpaced rate-base growth at IPL and WPL. Alliant reaffirmed 2026 ongoing EPS guidance of $3.36-$3.46, trending in the upper half.
summary_long: Second-quarter GAAP EPS of $0.65 fell from $0.68 a year ago and $0.87 in Q1, as $0.09/share of rate-base growth each at IPL and WPL plus higher equity income from venture investments were offset by higher O&M (labor, planned maintenance, new resources), higher financing and depreciation expense, an estimated $0.03/share temperature drag, and income-tax timing. Six-month ongoing (non-GAAP) EPS of $1.47 excluded a $0.05/share benefit from remeasuring deferred tax assets. Alliant reaffirmed full-year 2026 ongoing EPS guidance of $3.36-$3.46, trending in the upper half. Cash fell to $25M from $556M as the company retired $1,075M of long-term debt; six-month capex ran $1,022M.

drivers.explanation: Rate-base growth at IPL and WPL (+$0.09/share each) and higher equity income from corporate venture investments were more than offset by higher O&M, financing, and depreciation expense.
Temperature-driven demand cut about $0.03/share in Q2 2026 versus a $0.02/share benefit in Q2 2025, roughly a $0.05/share y/y swing.
Income-tax timing and higher interest/depreciation expense from continued capital investment also weighed on the quarter, per the release's earnings bridge.
Non-GAAP EPS excludes a $0.05/share benefit from remeasuring deferred tax assets tied to a state income-tax apportionment change; GAAP six-month EPS was $1.52.
